## 1. What We're Solving

Two separate crises, both urgent:

**Crisis A — New users (0% activation)**
547 total users. 0/14, 0/20, 0/21 new users in three daily cohorts ever generated an image.
Free welcome credits handed out, never used. The product is invisible to them.

**Crisis B — Membership retention (76% dormant)**
17 Studio members. 13 are silent. €97/month and they're not opening the app.
The product isn't giving them a reason to return.

These are different problems with different solutions. The plan addresses both.

## 2. Corrected Mode Architecture (Read Before Any UX Work)

### IMPORTANT: The Classic / Pro naming is wrong and must be fixed

Current code names are confusing and misleading. This must be resolved before Codex builds any UX that references mode names.

**How the modes actually work:**

| Code name | Model used | Who can access | What it needs |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|---------------|
| "Pro" tab | Nano Banana Pro (Replicate) | ALL users (free + membership) | Reference selfie(s) uploaded each session |
| "Classic" tab | Custom Flux LoRA (user-trained) | Currently membership-only | User's trained model (Training tab) |
| Mode toggle visible | Switch between the two | Membership users only | `showModeToggle = isMembership` |

**The problem:** "Pro" implies premium/advanced. "Classic" implies basic/old. Reality is the opposite — "Pro" (Nano Banana) is the accessible default everyone uses. "Classic" (custom Flux) is the advanced trained model. The names actively confuse users.

**✅ CONFIRMED: Option A — "SELFIE" / "MY MODEL"**
- "Pro" → **"SELFIE"** (you upload a selfie)
- "Classic" → **"MY MODEL"** (you use your trained model)

Most immediately understandable for the target audience. Every woman knows what a selfie is. "My Model" signals ownership and personal investment.

Codex rename scope: `activeMayaTab` values, tab label strings, any copy referencing "Classic mode" or "Pro mode". Zero logic changes — rename only.

## 3. The Access Model (Definitive — Corrected)

### What ALL users get (free, one-time, mini-product buyers)
- Maya chat (conversational AI with brand profile injected)
- **"Selfie" mode (Nano Banana Pro)**: upload a selfie as reference → generates photos that look like them. This is the primary mode for everyone.
- Credits gated (free users get welcome bonus; one-time credit purchases available)
- Mini-product workflows (if purchased): brand strategy, captions, offer builder, prompt library

### What Studio members get additionally (€97/month)
- **"My Model" mode (custom Flux)**: their trained AI model, no reference needed each session, most consistent results
- Mode toggle (switch between Selfie and My Model)
- Training tab: upload 10–15 selfies → train custom Flux LoRA model (costs 20 credits)
- Monthly credits refresh
- Academy: courses, templates, monthly resource drops
- Feed Planner full access

### ✅ CONFIRMED — Training is available to ALL users (credits gate only)

**Decision:** Remove membership gate. ANY user with 20 credits can train their custom Flux model.

**Implementation (Codex scope):**
- Remove `hasStudioMembership` check from `app/api/training/start/route.ts` and `app/api/training/start-training/route.ts`
- Show Training tab to ALL users (currently hidden for non-members)
- If user has insufficient credits: show card "Training costs 20 credits. [Buy credits →] or [Join Studio for monthly credits →]"
- Free users with purchased credits can train immediately
- Credit purchase incentive: "20 credits = your personal AI model"

**Why this works:** Training requires 20 credits — free users with 2 welcome credits can't afford it without purchasing. The gate is already effectively credits-based. Users who invest in training become deeply invested → drives membership for monthly credit refreshes.

### What mini-products are (€17–€47) — Separate from membership

Mini-products solve CONTENT problems. Membership solves PERSONALIZATION + SYSTEM problems.

| Product | Problem solved | Where in Maya |
|---------|---------------|---------------|
| What To Say (€17) | "I don't know what to say" | Brand Strategy Pack in chat |
| Show Up (€27) | "I'm not consistent" | 7-day content plan in chat |
| Get Paid (€47) | "I can't monetise" | Offer builder in chat |
| AI Photo Prompts (€17) | "I don't know what to generate" | Prompts tab (unlocks full library) |

Mini-product purchase = unlock specific Maya workflow. Membership = unlock the full system + personalization depth.

## 4. The Two User Journeys (Design North Stars)

### Journey A: New Free User → First Image → Upgrade Path

```
Sign up
  ↓
Maya opens — SELFIE tab (Nano Banana Pro, everyone's default)
  ↓
EMPTY STATE: "Start with your brand" (guided form, no credits needed)
  → Niche / audience / tone input
  → Maya generates: positioning + 3 pillars + 5 captions (text output, free)
  ↓
"Now let's see what you look like to the world"
  → Upload a selfie (reference image for Nano Banana Pro)
  → 3 example image prompts: 01 / 02 / 03 (no emojis)
  → User generates first image using free credits
  → "That's you. In seconds."
  ↓
POST-IMAGE CARD (free user):
  → "Want even better results?"
  → "Train your personal AI model — it learns your face and runs forever."
  → "20 credits to train. Buy credits →" OR "Join Studio for monthly credits →"
  ↓
Feed Planner CTA: "Build your first 9-post feed with this →"
```

### Journey B: New Studio Member → My Model Setup → Monthly Loop

```
Join Studio
  ↓
STUDIO MEMBER ONBOARDING (new — not generic onboarding):
  Step 1: "Your Studio is ready."
          → Credits balance, Selfie mode ON, Training available
  Step 2: "Start generating right now — upload one selfie"
          → SELFIE mode ImageUploadFlow → first generation → "That's you."
  Step 3: "Level up: train your personal AI model"
          → "10–15 photos, ~30 mins, runs forever"
          → "Start training →" OR "I'll do this later"
  ↓
RETURNING MEMBER (monthly ritual — not blank chat):
  → "[X] credits ready"
  → "This month's style drop: [preview]"
  → "Continue where you left off: [last session]"
  ↓
MONTHLY LOOP: Credits refresh → new drop → generate → feed → repeat
```

### PHASE 0 — Backend P0 Fixes (START IMMEDIATELY — parallel sprint)
*Estimated: 1–2 days. Source: Codex backend audit 2026-02-28.*

#### P0-01: Fix tab-sync + product-card navigation
**Files:** `components/sselfie/sselfie-app.tsx:144`, `components/sselfie/product-access-card.tsx:43`
**Problem:** URL `?tab=` updates but active tab state initialised once, not synced after param changes. Click product card → nothing happens.
**Fix:** Sync tab state from URL params reactively (useEffect on param change).
**Done when:** Click any product card → correct tab activates. `?tab=maya` always opens Maya.

#### P0-02: Complete product context into Maya
**Files:** `app/studio/page.tsx:151`, `components/sselfie/sselfie-app.tsx:1187`, `components/sselfie/maya/hooks/use-maya-chat.ts:155`
**Problem:** `first_time_product_user` not parsed/passed from Studio page. Product-specific Maya context not fully passed through render path.
**Fix:** Parse `first_time_product_user` from Studio page → SselfieApp → MayaChatScreen → use-maya-chat. Confirm product prop reaches Maya system prompt injection.
**Done when:** New product purchaser enters Maya → system prompt reflects their product → Maya greets with product-specific guidance.

#### P0-03: Fix analytics contract (MOST CRITICAL — can't measure activation otherwise)
**Files:** `lib/analytics/events.ts:19`, `components/sselfie/maya/welcome-first-generation-flow.tsx:67`, `components/onboarding/unified-onboarding-wizard.tsx:414`, `app/api/analytics/event/route.ts:65`
**Problem:** Unsupported event names emitted, silently ignored. Activation events dropping. TTFI not tracked end-to-end.
**Fix:** Add missing event names to supported list. Ensure `first_image_generated`, `onboarding_complete`, `credits_used`, `mode_selected` events fire. Add TTFI start on Maya tab load, TTFI complete on first image save to gallery.
**Done when:** Test user signs up → all activation events visible in analytics. TTFI measurable as single metric.

#### P0-04: Broadcast preflight + bounce cleanup
**Files:** `app/api/admin/marketing/brand-engine-broadcast/send/route.ts:45`, `lib/email/send-newsletter-broadcast.ts:147`
**Problem:** Send path lacks non-zero-recipient preflight. 1,965 hard bounces in list.
**Fix:** Add recipient count > 0 check before status transitions. Suppress bounce addresses from all sends.
**Done when:** Broadcast with zero valid recipients fails safely. Bounce list excluded from sends.

## 8. Parallel Agent Execution Guide (For North + ClawdBot)

**How SSELFIE's agent system actually works:**

This is NOT Claude Code background agents. The parallelism in this system runs through **ClawdBot** — the custom multi-agent orchestration platform Sandra has built on her Mac.

### The agent roster (ClawdBot)

| Agent ID | Role | What it does |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `north` | COO orchestrator | Reads priorities, delegates, coordinates handoffs |
| `north-code` | Technical PM | Writes Codex specs, runs Codex, monitors Vercel deploys |
| `north-content` | Content writer | Captions, emails, copy — in Sandra's exact voice |
| `north-revenue` | Revenue analyst | MRR checks, Stripe data, churn analysis |
| `north-audience` | Researcher | Competitor analysis, trend spotting, audience language |
| `north-product` | HTML builder | Takes content briefs → builds polished HTML Academy products |

**maxConcurrent: 3** — ClawdBot runs up to 3 subagents simultaneously.

### How North spawns a subagent

```bash
clawdbot agent --agent [id] --message "[task description]"
```

Example:
```bash
clawdbot agent --agent north-code --message "Read ~/stella/tasks/codex-p0-fixes.md and queue all 4 Codex specs in order"
clawdbot agent --agent north-content --message "Read ~/stella/tasks/CONTENT-email-dormant-members.md and draft the re-engagement email"
clawdbot agent --agent north-revenue --message "Pull Stripe MRR and count how many Studio members have been silent for 30+ days"
```

### How north-code runs Codex (the exact protocol)

north-code does NOT write code itself. It:
1. Writes a Codex spec to `~/stella/tasks/codex-[name].md`
2. Runs: `codex --approval-mode full-auto --quiet "Read ~/stella/tasks/codex-[name].md and implement it exactly"`
3. Waits for completion
4. Verifies: checks `git log`, checks Vercel deploy, tests the route
5. If Vercel fails: diagnoses → writes a fix spec → runs Codex again
6. Updates `~/stella/SHARED_MEMORY.md` with result

**Codex runs ONE spec at a time** (sequential within north-code). Multiple Codex specs must queue.

### The parallel execution model

True parallelism in this system is:

```
north-code (running Codex specs sequentially)
    +
north-content (writing copy in parallel)
    +
north-revenue OR north-audience (research/data in parallel)
```

All three run simultaneously via ClawdBot (maxConcurrent: 3). The three lanes are independent — code work, content work, and data work don't block each other.

### How to structure the full sprint in ClawdBot

**North's session prompt to kick off the plan:**

```
Read ~/stella/NORTH_TASK_QUEUE.md and ~/stella/SHARED_MEMORY.md first.

Then delegate this sprint in parallel:

1. Spawn north-code:
   "Write Codex specs for P0-01, P0-02, P0-03, P0-04, and UX-01.
    Save each to ~/stella/tasks/codex-[taskid].md using the specs in
    ~/stella/tasks/MASTER-PLAN-2026-02-28.md Section 4.
    Run them in order: P0-01 → P0-02 → P0-03 → P0-04 → UX-01.
    Update SHARED_MEMORY.md after each completes."

2. Spawn north-revenue:
   "Check Stripe. How many Studio members are active vs dormant (no login in 30 days)?
    List their names and last active dates. Save to ~/stella/reports/dormant-members-[date].md"

3. Spawn north-content:
   "Read MASTER-PLAN-2026-02-28.md Phase 5 email specs.
    Draft the dormant member re-engagement email in Sandra's voice.
    Save to ~/stella/drafts/email-dormant-reengagement.md"

Wait for all three to complete. Then report status.
```

### Codex spec template (north-code uses this for every spec)

```markdown
# Codex Task: [task-id] — [task name]
# Written by: north-code | Date: [date]

## Context
[1-2 sentences: what this fixes and why it matters]

## Visual Reference
[path to HTML prototype, or "none"]

## Files to modify
- [file 1] — [what to change]
- [file 2] — [what to change]

## Files to create (if any)
- [new file path] — [purpose]

## Files you must NEVER touch
- app/api/** (all API routes — zero changes)
- lib/credits.ts, lib/subscription.ts (business logic — no changes)
- Any hook file not explicitly listed above

## Exact changes required
[Precise spec from MASTER-PLAN or DESIGN-SPRINT tasks — paste in full]

## Done when
1. [acceptance criterion 1]
2. [acceptance criterion 2]
3. pnpm build passes with zero TypeScript errors
4. Component renders correctly at 375px viewport width
5. No console errors

## Do not
- Change any API endpoints or their request/response shape
- Modify any Stripe, credits, or subscription logic
- Add new dependencies without flagging for review
```

### Agent handoff protocol

When north-code finishes a Queue, it updates `~/stella/SHARED_MEMORY.md` APP STATE section so north-content knows it's safe to reference new feature names in copy. When north-revenue identifies dormant members, it writes to `~/stella/reports/` so north-content can personalise the re-engagement email. This shared memory is how parallel agents coordinate without blocking each other.

   - All 4 products (What To Say, Show Up, Get Paid, AI Photo Prompts) are included for ALL current and new Studio members
